docs.title: Home
docs.text:
CLI-FIRST AI RESEARCH ASSISTANT One Command. Search. Reason. Answer.

Zuni brings AI-powered research to your terminal. Ask a question, let Zuni search the web when needed, and get a grounded answer without leaving your workflow.

Get Started → View on GitHub zuni 
$ zuni ask "What is quantum computing?"

→ web_search: quantum computing
→ extract_markdown: https://...

Quantum computing uses quantum-mechanical phenomena
to process information in ways that differ from
classical computing. [1]

Sources
[1] Source title
    https://...
WHY ZUNI Research without leavingthe terminal.

Zuni combines an OpenAI-compatible LLM client with a small tool-calling agent and web research tools.

⚡ One Command

Ask a question directly from the terminal and let Zuni handle the research loop.

⌕ Web Research

Search DuckDuckGo and read selected pages when current or factual information is needed.

◈ Grounded Answers

Sources are numbered and can be cited inline so you can inspect where an answer came from.

THE FLOW Question to answer,through tools. 01 Ask

Write your question.

→ 02 Research

The model can call search and page-reading tools.

→ 03 Answer

Zuni returns a Markdown response with sources.

GET STARTED OPEN SOURCE Built in the open.

Zuni is an evolving project. Explore the code, follow the roadmap, or contribute to its development.

GitHub ↗ START EXPLORING Open your terminal.

The web is huge. Your command can stay simple.

Get Started →

docs.title: Meet Zuni in one command.
docs.text:
zuni ask "Explain how DNS works"

By default, Zuni can use its research tools. To ask the model directly:

zuni ask --no-search "Explain recursion"

Read the documentation →

docs.title: What is Zuni?
docs.text: Zuni is a command-line AI research assistant. It sends questions to an OpenAI-compatible model and can use web-search tools to gather information before producing an answer.

docs.title: Does Zuni search the web?
docs.text:
Yes. Web research is enabled by default for zuni ask. The model can use web_search to search DuckDuckGo and extract_markdown to read a specific public page.

Use --no-search to bypass the research workflow.

docs.title: Does every model support tool calling?
docs.text: No. Tool calling depends on the model/provider. If the first tool-enabled request fails, Zuni falls back to a simpler search-first flow: search the web, collect sources, then send them to the model in a normal request.

docs.title: Is Zuni free?
docs.text: The Zuni software is open source under the MIT License. Your model provider may charge for API usage.

docs.title: Which providers work?
docs.text: Zuni targets providers with an OpenAI-compatible POST /chat/completions endpoint. Tool calling additionally requires support for the tools request format.

docs.title: Does Zuni store my questions?
docs.text: Zuni stores its configuration locally and does not implement a server-side conversation database. Requests sent to hosted model or web services are subject to those services' privacy policies.

docs.title: Where is my API key stored?
docs.text:
By default, the key entered through zuni config is stored in:

~/.config/zuni/config.json

You can override it with ZUNI_API_KEY. Protect the config file and never commit it.

docs.title: Can I use a local model?
docs.text:
Yes, if the local server exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint. For example:

http://localhost:11434/v1

Use --no-search if you do not want Zuni to access the web.

docs.title: Can I use Zuni offline?
docs.text: The direct LLM path can work without internet when the configured model server is reachable locally. Web research requires network access.

docs.title: How does citation work?
docs.text:
Zuni assigns numbers to collected sources:

[1] First source
[2] Second source

The model is instructed to cite those numbers inline. Zuni then prints the corresponding URLs below the answer.

docs.title: How do I control search results?
docs.text:
zuni ask -n 3 "Your question"

The allowed range is 1 to 10.

docs.title: How do I change the model?
docs.text: Run zuni config or edit ~/.config/zuni/config.json. You can also override the base URL with ZUNI_BASE_URL.

docs.title: Where can I contribute?
docs.text: See Contributing.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
Zuni is evolving from a small CLI question-answering tool into a compact terminal research assistant.

This roadmap describes the current direction. It is not a fixed release schedule.

docs.title: Available now
docs.text:
• zuni ask for one-command questions
  • zuni config for API key, model, and base URL
  • OpenAI-compatible chat-completions support
  • Markdown rendering in the terminal
  • Async HTTP requests
  • Retry handling for temporary LLM API failures
  • Agent/tool-calling loop
  • DuckDuckGo web search
  • Web-page extraction to Markdown
  • Numbered source tracking and citations
  • Fallback search flow for models without tool calling
  • --no-search direct-answer mode

docs.title: In progress
docs.text:
• Stronger validation of model-generated tool calls
  • More robust URL and redirect safety
  • Automated tests for configuration, tools, citations, and the agent loop
  • Better documentation and API reference

docs.title: Planned
docs.text:
• Streaming responses
  • Conversation mode
  • Reading input from stdin
  • Multiple saved profiles
  • CI pipeline
  • PyPI release

docs.title: Ideas
docs.text:
• Shell completions
  • JSON and other structured output modes
  • Additional research tools
  • Local/offline-first workflows
  • More provider-specific configuration options

Note

The roadmap can change as Zuni's architecture and goals evolve.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions are welcome across code, documentation, bug fixes, and ideas.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/ssannssarr/Zuni.git
cd Zuni
uv sync
uv run zuni --help

For a global editable installation:

uv tool install --editable .

docs.title: Preview the documentation
docs.text: uv run mkdocs serve

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository.
  2. Create a focused branch.
  3. Make the change.
  4. Run relevant commands locally.
  5. Update documentation when behavior changes.
  6. Commit with a clear message.
  7. Push and open a pull request.

Example branch:

git checkout -b feature/my-change

docs.title: Commit messages
docs.text:
feat: add streaming responses
fix: handle missing config file
docs: expand installation guide
refactor: simplify tool dispatch
Prefix Use for feat New features fix Bug fixes docs Documentation refactor Internal restructuring

docs.title: Code guidelines
docs.text:
• Keep functions focused.
  • Use type hints.
  • Prefer async APIs for network operations.
  • Keep user-facing errors understandable.
  • Do not commit API keys or local configuration files.
  • Be careful when changing model-controlled network access.

docs.title: Tool and web-search changes
docs.text:
When modifying a tool:

  • keep its schema and implementation consistent
  • validate required arguments
  • preserve useful error messages
  • avoid exposing secrets in tool output
  • consider URL and redirect safety
  • update the architecture documentation

docs.title: Documentation guidelines
docs.text:
• Document current behavior, not planned behavior.
  • Keep examples runnable.
  • Keep pages short and scannable.
  • Update links when pages move.
  • Keep architecture documentation synchronized with the code.

docs.title: Useful contribution areas
docs.text: Current areas that can use work include stronger agent tests, configuration handling, URL safety, error handling, documentation, CI, and packaging.

docs.title: Reporting a bug
docs.text:
Open an issue and include:

  • command you ran
  • full error output
  • OS and Python version
  • Zuni version or commit
  • relevant configuration with secrets removed

Warning

Never include API keys, access tokens, or private configuration values in an issue.

docs.title: License
docs.text: By contributing, you agree that your contribution is released under the project's MIT License.

docs.title: Core modules
docs.text: Path Purpose src/zuni/cli.py CLI commands, execution flow, and output rendering src/zuni/agent.py Tool-calling loop src/zuni/errors.py Zuni exception types src/zuni/llm/config.py Configuration loading and saving src/zuni/llm/llm.py OpenAI-compatible API client src/zuni/prompts/prompt.py Prompt loading src/zuni/prompts/system.md Base system prompt src/zuni/search/search.py HTTP requests and DuckDuckGo parsing src/zuni/tools/schema.py Tool definitions sent to the model src/zuni/tools/toolbox.py Tool dispatch and source tracking src/zuni/tools/web_search.py Search plus page enrichment src/zuni/tools/extract_markdown.py HTML-to-Markdown extraction

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text:
pyproject.toml contains package metadata, runtime dependencies, the Python requirement, and the zuni console-script entry point:

[project.scripts]
zuni = "zuni.cli:main"

The repository's .python-version currently uses Python 3.14 for development, while package metadata supports Python 3.11+.

docs.title: Adding or changing a command
docs.text:
1. Update the command in src/zuni/cli.py.
  2. Test it with uv run zuni ....
  3. Update Commands.
  4. Update architecture documentation if the execution flow changed.

docs.title: Adding a tool
docs.text:
A tool has three important pieces:

  1. Schema in src/zuni/tools/schema.py.
  2. Execution in src/zuni/tools/toolbox.py.
  3. Implementation in the relevant search/tool module.

The schema name and dispatcher name must match.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Run the local documentation server with:

uv run mkdocs serve

When code behavior changes, update the corresponding documentation page in the same change whenever possible.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Zuni uses an OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions API. OpenRouter is the default base URL when no base URL is supplied.

docs.title: Interactive setup
docs.text:
zuni config

Zuni asks for three values:

Prompt Description Example API key Credential used for the model API sk-or-v1-... Model ID Model identifier accepted by your provider openrouter/free Base URL API root, without /chat/completions https://openrouter.ai/api/v1

The values are saved to:

~/.config/zuni/config.json

docs.title: Config file
docs.text:
{
    "API_KEY": "your-api-key",
    "MODEL": "openrouter/free",
    "BASE_URL": "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"
}

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Purpose ZUNI_API_KEY Overrides API_KEY from the config file ZUNI_BASE_URL Overrides BASE_URL from the config file Bash / ZshFishPowerShell 
export ZUNI_API_KEY="your-api-key"
export ZUNI_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"

set -Ux ZUNI_API_KEY "your-api-key"
set -Ux ZUNI_BASE_URL "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"

$env:ZUNI_API_KEY = "your-api-key"
$env:ZUNI_BASE_URL = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"

docs.title: API key
docs.text:
1. ZUNI_API_KEY
  2. API_KEY in config.json
  3. Error

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
1. MODEL in config.json
  2. openrouter/free

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text:
1. ZUNI_BASE_URL
  2. BASE_URL in config.json
  3. OpenRouter's default URL in the LLM client

Note

Running zuni config once is the simplest setup because Zuni reads the model and base URL from the configuration module.

docs.title: Provider examples
docs.text:
OpenRouterOpenAILocal Ollama 
Base URL: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
Model ID: openrouter/free

Base URL: https://api.openai.com/v1
Model ID: <your-model>

Any provider that accepts the OpenAI-compatible POST /chat/completions format can be used. Tool calling additionally depends on model/provider support.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Warning

Never commit your API key or config.json to Git. If a key leaks, revoke it from your provider immediately.

On Linux, macOS, and Termux:

chmod 600 ~/.config/zuni/config.json

docs.title: Reset configuration
docs.text:
rm ~/.config/zuni/config.json
zuni config

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Zuni is an asynchronous CLI built around an OpenAI-compatible LLM client, a small tool-calling agent, and web research tools.

docs.title: High-level flow
docs.text:
zuni ask
   │
   ▼
 cli.py
   │
   ├── --no-search ──► LLM ──► Markdown
   │
   └── search mode
          │
          ▼
       Agent loop
          │
      ┌───┴───────────┐
      ▼               ▼
 web_search     extract_markdown
      │               │
      └───────┬───────┘
              ▼
          tool results
              │
              ▼
             LLM
              │
              ▼
       Markdown + sources

docs.title: cli.py
docs.text: The CLI defines commands, loads configuration and prompts, creates the LLM client and Toolbox, selects direct or research mode, handles the no-tool-calling fallback, renders Markdown, and prints sources.

docs.title: agent.py
docs.text:
run_agent() implements the tool-calling loop:

LLM request
    ↓
assistant message
    ↓
tool_calls?
  ├─ no → final answer
  └─ yes
       ↓
Toolbox.run(...)
       ↓
tool result appended to chat
       ↓
LLM request again

The current agent has a default maximum of four tool-call rounds. When that budget is exhausted, Zuni asks the model to answer using the information gathered so far.

If the first tool-enabled request fails, the CLI treats that as possible lack of tool support and uses the search-first fallback.

docs.title: llm/llm.py
docs.text:
The LLM class builds OpenAI-compatible chat-completion requests, optionally attaches tool definitions, sends them asynchronously with httpx, retries temporary failures, maps API errors, and extracts assistant messages.

Requests are sent to:

{BASE_URL}/chat/completions

docs.title: llm/config.py
docs.text: Configuration lives at ~/.config/zuni/config.json. The module resolves the API key, model, and base URL from the config file and supported environment variables.

docs.title: tools/schema.py
docs.text:
This module defines the tool schemas sent to the model.

Tool Purpose web_search Search DuckDuckGo and return numbered sources extract_markdown Download a specific public page and extract readable Markdown

docs.title: tools/toolbox.py
docs.text: Toolbox is the execution layer between model tool calls and Python functions. It parses arguments, dispatches tool names, tracks sources, assigns source numbers, and returns tool failures as text.

docs.title: tools/web_search.py
docs.text: The web-search tool combines DuckDuckGo results with best-effort fetching of the top pages and converts fetched HTML into compact Markdown. Up to three page downloads run concurrently.

docs.title: search/search.py
docs.text: This module handles lower-level HTTP requests, DuckDuckGo HTML parsing, and public URL checks before page fetching.

docs.title: tools/extract_markdown.py
docs.text: HTML is cleaned by removing common noise such as scripts, navigation, forms, and iframes. Zuni prefers article, main, or body content and converts it to compact Markdown.

docs.title: Sources and citations
docs.text:
Sources are represented as:

Source(index, title, url, content)

Toolbox owns the source list. A source receives a number when first registered. Repeated URLs reuse the existing source number.

The final model response can cite sources as [1], [2], and so on. The CLI extracts those references and prints the corresponding URLs below the answer.

docs.title: Direct mode
docs.text:
zuni ask --no-search "Explain recursion"

Direct mode skips the agent and tools:

CLI → system prompt + question → LLM → Markdown

docs.title: Design goals
docs.text:
• CLI first: keep the interface small and terminal-friendly.
  • Async: network operations use asynchronous APIs.
  • Provider neutral: use the common OpenAI-compatible chat-completions format.
  • Tool based: keep web capabilities behind explicit model-callable tools.
  • Grounded: preserve source information so answers can cite retrieved material.
  • Small core: keep the agent and tool layer understandable.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Zuni currently exposes two commands:

zuni [COMMAND] [ARGUMENTS]
Command Purpose zuni ask Ask a question and optionally research the web zuni config Save API key, model, and base URL zuni --help Show command help

docs.title: zuni ask
docs.text:
Ask a question from the terminal.

zuni ask "Explain how DNS works"

Web research is enabled by default. The agent can decide to use the available tools, then return an answer with cited sources.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: zuni ask [OPTIONS] PROMPT...

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Description --no-search Skip the agent/tool workflow and ask the model directly -n, --results INTEGER Maximum number of search results to use, from 1 to 10; default: 5

The prompt can contain multiple shell arguments. Zuni joins them into one question.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
ResearchDirect modelControl result count 
zuni ask "What are the latest changes in Python?"
zuni ask "Compare HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2"

zuni ask --no-search "Explain recursion"
zuni ask --no-search "Write a Python function that reverses a string"

zuni ask -n 3 "What is quantum computing?"
zuni ask --results 8 "Compare current Linux distributions"

docs.title: How a researched question works
docs.text:
1. Zuni loads the system prompt and configuration.
  2. The LLM receives the question plus the available tool definitions.
  3. The model may call web_search.
  4. Zuni runs the requested tool and sends the result back to the model.
  5. The model may call extract_markdown to read a specific page.
  6. The agent repeats the tool loop until the model answers or the step budget is reached.
  7. Zuni renders the Markdown answer.
  8. Cited sources are printed below the answer.

If the selected model does not support tool calling, Zuni falls back to a simpler flow: search first, then send the collected sources to the model.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
When web research is used, Zuni numbers sources:

[1] Source title
URL: https://example.com/...
Source content...

[2] Another source
URL: https://example.org/...
Source content...

The model can cite them as [1], [2], etc. Zuni then prints the cited sources at the bottom of the response.

docs.title: Quoting tips
docs.text:
Quote questions containing shell characters:

zuni ask 'What does $PATH do?'
zuni ask "What is Python's GIL?"

docs.title: Save an answer
docs.text:
zuni ask "List five Linux commands" > answer.txt

Terminal Markdown styling is not preserved in redirected output.

docs.title: Alias
docs.text:
alias z='zuni ask'
z "What is a mutex?"

docs.title: zuni config
docs.text:
Interactively saves configuration:

zuni config

See Configuration for details.

docs.title: Help
docs.text:
zuni --help
zuni ask --help
zuni config --help

docs.title: zuni: command not found
docs.text:
Update uv's shell integration:

uv tool update-shell

Restart the terminal and try again.

docs.title: Configuration file error
docs.text:
If you see Configuration File doesn't exists!, run:

zuni config

Zuni stores configuration at ~/.config/zuni/config.json.

docs.title: API key error
docs.text:
Set the current environment variable:

export ZUNI_API_KEY="your-api-key"

or run zuni config. The current implementation checks ZUNI_API_KEY, not OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

docs.title: Authentication errors
docs.text: For HTTP 401 or 403 responses, verify the API key, provider, and model access.

docs.title: Model or provider errors
docs.text: Zuni sends requests to {BASE_URL}/chat/completions. Check MODEL and BASE_URL in your configuration.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text: The LLM client retries temporary failures including HTTP 429 and common 5xx responses. If the provider continues returning errors, wait or change models.

docs.title: Connection or timeout errors
docs.text: Check your internet connection, base URL, provider availability, firewall, and VPN. The LLM client uses a 60-second default timeout and retries temporary failures.

docs.title: Web search fails
docs.text:
DuckDuckGo may rate-limit automated requests. If search is unavailable, Zuni can return the tool error to the model or use its search-first fallback when tool calling is unavailable.

For questions that do not need research:

zuni ask --no-search "Explain recursion"

docs.title: The model does not support tools
docs.text:
Not every OpenAI-compatible model supports tool calling. When the first tool-enabled request fails, Zuni falls back to:

web search → collect sources → normal LLM request

docs.title: Answers have no citations
docs.text:
Citations depend on the model using the source numbers supplied by Zuni. Check that web research ran and inspect the source list printed below the answer.

Zuni only accepts citation numbers that correspond to collected sources.

docs.title: A page cannot be fetched
docs.text: Zuni rejects obvious local/private/non-HTTP(S) targets when reading model-selected URLs. Public pages can still fail because of anti-bot protection, authentication, redirects, network errors, or unusual HTML.

docs.title: Python version
docs.text:
Package metadata supports Python 3.11+. The repository currently uses Python 3.14 for development.

python --version

docs.title: Debug mode
docs.text:
Set ZUNI_DEBUG to let unexpected exceptions propagate:

ZUNI_DEBUG=1 zuni ask "your question"

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text: Open an issue and include the command, full error, OS, Python version, and relevant configuration with secrets removed. Never post your API key.
